title: The Bible
description: Position 4 in Most Mainstream-Loved Books Ever Written, owner-supplied 14 September 2026 synthesis. Attribution: Multiple authors; Jewish and Christian scriptural traditions. First publication/textual period: Ancient texts; canon varies. Repeated devotional engagement, worldwide scriptural access and a high German public-vote placement establish an extraordinary continuing relationship with this collection. American Bible Society research adds a contemporary, geographically limited engagement signal. This position compares unlike forms of attachment: religious observance and affection for a novel. Copies distributed and numbers of religious adherents are not treated as readers who love it.

title: The Quran
description: Position 5 in Most Mainstream-Loved Books Ever Written, owner-supplied 14 September 2026 synthesis. Attribution: Islamic scripture; traditionally revealed to Muhammad. First publication/textual period: 7th century. Pew's multinational research documents frequent reading of, or listening to, the Quran in diverse Muslim societies. That continuing practice is unusually strong evidence of durable textual attachment across cultures. Its placement remains a cross-category judgment: devotional commitment cannot be converted into favourite-novel votes, and neither religious identity nor compulsory study is counted as proof of voluntary affection.

title: One Thousand and One Nights / The Arabian Nights
original_language: Arabic, with Persian, Indian and other roots
description: Position 34 in Most Mainstream-Loved Books Ever Written, owner-supplied 14 September 2026 synthesis. Attribution: Multiple storytellers and compilers. First publication/textual period: Medieval compilation; recensions vary. The collection's translation and adaptation history, together with modern reader enthusiasm, supports extraordinary narrative endurance across Arabic and many other traditions. Its changing contents make comparison especially difficult: different editions contain different stories, and famous additions are not present in every Arabic manuscript tradition. The ranked unit is the recognised collection, with that instability explicitly retained.
